title: The Empty Nest
story: A robin built a nest in the bush outside Room 9. The class watched three blue eggs every day. One morning, the eggs were gone! Pieces of blue shell were at the bottom of the nest. The class heard tiny cheep-cheep sounds. Three fuzzy baby birds poked their heads up with their mouths open. No cats or snakes were seen near the bush. "The eggs didn’t disappear," said Mr. Gold. "They hatched!"
question: What happened to the robin eggs?

suspects.why: pieces of shell, baby birds cheeping
no cats were seen near the bush
no snakes were seen

answer: The robin eggs hatched.
proof: "Pieces of blue shell were at the bottom of the nest."
"Three fuzzy baby birds poked their heads up with their mouths open."
clears: Cat or snake: "No cats or snakes were seen near the bush."
explain: This shows the eggs hatched because there are broken shells and baby birds in the nest. Because of this, the eggs turned into baby robins. (Science link: life cycles.)

title: The Earth Day Litter Mystery
story: For Earth Day, the class went to clean up Maple Park. They found trash all around the picnic table! The trash can lid was off, and the bag inside was ripped open. Wrappers had little bite marks on them. Muddy paw prints with five fingers led to the creek. The park ranger said she emptied the can last week and closed the lid tight. That evening, a raccoon family came out to dig in the can again.
question: Who made the mess at the park?

suspects.why: ripped bag, bite marks, five-finger prints
closed the lid tight
they came to clean it up

answer: Raccoons made the mess at the park.
proof: "Wrappers had little bite marks on them."
"Muddy paw prints with five fingers led to the creek."
clears: Ranger: "The park ranger said she emptied the can last week and closed the lid tight."
explain: This shows raccoons got into the trash because the wrappers were bitten and their prints led away. Because of this, raccoons made the mess.

title: The Lost Field Trip Camera
story: At the zoo, Ms. Ray took pictures with the class camera. When the class got back on the bus, the camera was gone! Ms. Ray checked her bag and her coat pockets. Then Ty remembered that she set it on the bench by the penguins to tie her shoe. The zoo worker at the penguin house found a camera on that bench. The bus driver had stayed on the bus the whole time. The monkeys were in a closed cage far away.
question: Where did the camera go?

suspects.why: Ty saw her set it there, worker found it there
in a closed cage far away
stayed on the bus the whole time

answer: Ms. Ray left the camera on the bench by the penguins.
proof: "Then Ty remembered that she set it on the bench by the penguins to tie her shoe."
"The zoo worker at the penguin house found a camera on that bench."
clears: Monkeys: "The monkeys were in a closed cage far away."
Driver: "The bus driver had stayed on the bus the whole time."
explain: This shows the camera was on the bench because Ty saw her set it there and a worker found it there. Because of this, the camera was left behind, not stolen.

title: The Droopy Bean Plant
story: The class planted bean seeds in cups. Every plant grew tall and green, except one. Jin’s plant was pale yellow and droopy. His cup had been moved into the dark supply closet to make room for a project. The other cups sat on the sunny windowsill. Jin watered his plant every day, and the soil was still wet. After one week back by the window, his plant turned green again.
question: Why was Jin’s plant pale and droopy?

suspects.why: moved into the dark closet, green again by the window
he watered every day, soil was wet
it grew again by the window

answer: Jin’s plant did not get sunlight.
proof: "His cup had been moved into the dark supply closet to make room for a project."
"After one week back by the window, his plant turned green again."
clears: Water: "Jin watered his plant every day, and the soil was still wet."
explain: This shows the plant needed light because it turned green again in the sun. Because of this, being in the dark closet made it pale. (Science link: what plants need.)

title: The Melted Ice Cream
story: For the end-of-unit party, Mr. Fox bought ice cream and put it in the teacher lounge freezer. At 2:00, the ice cream was soup! The freezer door was open a crack, and a box of paper plates was stuck in it. Cold air was coming out into the room. Ms. Hall had put the paper plates on the top shelf that morning. The power was on, because the microwave and lights worked. "The door could not close!" said Mr. Fox.
question: Why did the ice cream melt?

suspects.why: door open a crack, plates stuck in it
the microwave and lights worked
it would have stayed frozen with the door closed

answer: The freezer door was left open, so the ice cream melted.
proof: "The freezer door was open a crack, and a box of paper plates was stuck in it."
"Cold air was coming out into the room."
clears: Power: "The power was on, because the microwave and lights worked."
explain: This shows the freezer could not stay cold because the door was blocked open. Because of this, the ice cream melted. (Science link: solid to liquid.)

title: The Field Day Ribbon
story: On Field Day, Maya won a blue first-place ribbon. She clipped it to her water bottle and went to the sack race. When she came back, the ribbon was gone! A gust of wind blew everyone’s hats around. Maya saw something blue flapping against the fence at the edge of the field. It was her ribbon, caught on the wire. Her friend Ally had been in the sack race with her the whole time. The coach had all the extra ribbons locked in a box.
question: What happened to Maya’s ribbon?

suspects.why: gust of wind, ribbon caught on the fence
in the sack race with her the whole time
extra ribbons were locked in a box

answer: The wind blew Maya’s ribbon to the fence.
proof: "A gust of wind blew everyone’s hats around."
"It was her ribbon, caught on the wire."
clears: Ally: "Her friend Ally had been in the sack race with her the whole time."
Coach: "The coach had all the extra ribbons locked in a box."
explain: This shows the wind carried the ribbon because it ended up on the fence after a big gust. Because of this, nobody took it.

title: The Popping Balloons
story: On the last day of school, the class tied balloons to the playground fence. One by one, they started to pop! The balloons were in the bright, hot sun, and the thermometer said 90 degrees. The balloons in the shade by the door were still fine. No one was near the fence, because everyone was eating popsicles under the tree. "The heat made the air inside get bigger!" said Ms. Jade.
question: Why did the balloons pop?

suspects.why: 90 degrees, sunny ones popped, shady ones were fine
everyone was under the tree
no clues point to birds

answer: The hot sun made the balloons pop.
proof: "The balloons were in the bright, hot sun, and the thermometer said 90 degrees."
"The balloons in the shade by the door were still fine."
clears: Students: "No one was near the fence, because everyone was eating popsicles under the tree."
explain: This shows the heat popped them because only the balloons in the sun popped. Because of this, the hot sun was the cause. (Science link: heat makes gas expand.)
